# MMSpower

![MMSpower hex logo](logo.svg)

# MMSpower

Sample size, power and analysis for malaria molecular surveillance
studies, allowing for imperfect diagnostic tests and sampling clustered
across sites.

[Get started](https://mrc-ide.github.io/MMSpower/articles/MMSpower.md)
[Tutorials](https://mrc-ide.github.io/MMSpower/articles/index.md)
[Reference](https://mrc-ide.github.io/MMSpower/reference/index.md)

## Why MMSpower

Malaria programmes increasingly use molecular surveillance, for example
of drug-resistance markers or *pfhrp2/3* deletions, to make decisions.
These surveys are often clustered across sites, rely on imperfect
assays, and need to be tailored to local constraints. MMSpower provides
straightforward functions for designing a study and analysing its
results, with a focus on malaria molecular surveillance (MMS)
applications.

## A first example

How many samples are needed to estimate a prevalence of around 30% to
within ±5 percentage points, sampling 10 people per site with an ICC of
0.05?

``` r

library(MMSpower)

design_precision(prevalence = 0.3, moe = 0.05, n_per_site = 10, icc = 0.05)
#> $n
#> [1] 500
#>
#> $n_sites
#> [1] 50
#>
#> $n_per_site
#> [1] 10
#>
#> $deff
#> [1] 1.45
#>
#> $n_eff
#> [1] 341
#>
#> $moe
#> [1] 0.04965355
```

50 sites of 10 people, giving a margin of error just under the 5-point
target. Without clustering, 341 people would be enough; the design
effect of 1.45 accounts for people at the same site resembling each
other.

The [tutorials](https://mrc-ide.github.io/MMSpower/articles/index.md)
take each type of study from design through to analysis, starting with
[estimating
prevalence](https://mrc-ide.github.io/MMSpower/articles/tutorial-prevalence.md).

## Installation

Install the latest release from GitHub with:

``` r

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("mrc-ide/MMSpower")
```

or the development version with
`remotes::install_github("mrc-ide/MMSpower@develop")`.

## About

MMSpower is developed by Sequoia Leuba and Bob Verity at Imperial
College London. The source code is on
[GitHub](https://github.com/mrc-ide/MMSpower), where you can also
[report issues](https://github.com/mrc-ide/MMSpower/issues).

# Package index

## Estimating prevalence

How many samples for a target margin of error, and the estimate with its
confidence interval.

- [`design_precision()`](https://mrc-ide.github.io/MMSpower/reference/design_precision.md)
  : Calculate sample size for a target margin of error when estimating
  prevalence
- [`estimate_prevalence()`](https://mrc-ide.github.io/MMSpower/reference/estimate_prevalence.md)
  : Estimate prevalence and its precision

## Testing against a threshold

Is prevalence above (or below) a decision threshold, such as the WHO
pfhrp2/3 deletion threshold?

- [`design_threshold()`](https://mrc-ide.github.io/MMSpower/reference/design_threshold.md)
  : Calculate sample size to detect a prevalence above or below a
  threshold
- [`test_threshold()`](https://mrc-ide.github.io/MMSpower/reference/test_threshold.md)
  : Test whether prevalence is above or below a decision threshold

## Detecting presence

How many samples to find at least one case of a rare variant, such as an
early drug-resistance marker?

- [`design_detection()`](https://mrc-ide.github.io/MMSpower/reference/design_detection.md)
  : Calculate sample size to detect at least one case

## Comparing two groups

Does prevalence differ between two groups, such as two regions?

- [`design_difference()`](https://mrc-ide.github.io/MMSpower/reference/design_difference.md)
  : Calculate sample size to detect a difference in prevalence between
  two groups
- [`test_difference()`](https://mrc-ide.github.io/MMSpower/reference/test_difference.md)
  : Test whether prevalence differs between two groups

## Costing a study

- [`estimate_cost()`](https://mrc-ide.github.io/MMSpower/reference/estimate_cost.md)
  : Estimate total study cost
